prompt:
Reports from several teams about workspaces that were closed from the danger-zone page.

1. Support: a customer closed their workspace a month ago. Its members still see it in their workspace list, can switch into it and open it, and have been working in it as if nothing had happened.
2. Support: after the closure, a person who had been invited earlier accepted the invitation and became a member of the closed workspace; the former owner then received a "new member joined" notification for it.
3. Notifications: reminders for overdue issues of the closed workspace are still being sent to the people they were assigned to.
4. Integrations: webhook deliveries that were waiting in the queue when the workspace was closed went out afterwards.
5. Billing: the closed workspace's trial ended a week later and the system recorded a plan change to the Free plan for it (visible in its audit log and sent to its webhooks). Its subscription is still shown as active.
6. Support: closing the same workspace a second time from a stale tab reported success again.

Expected behaviour. Closing a workspace is final and takes effect immediately, for everyone. The workspace disappears from every member's workspace list; nobody can open it or switch into it, not even with a session that was valid before, and nothing in it can be read through the app any more. No invitation to it can be accepted, whenever it was sent. Nothing is produced for it from then on: no notifications of any kind, no digest, no reminders, no webhook deliveries (including deliveries queued before the closing) and no plan changes recorded, because its subscription ends at the moment of closing. Background jobs skip it entirely, including a rebuild of its search index. Closing a workspace that is already closed is refused as a conflict, exactly as archiving an archived project is; a wrong confirmation refuses without closing anything. The address of a closed workspace stays reserved: a new workspace asking for that address gets a different one instead of an error. Other workspaces are unaffected, including those that share members with the closed one.

This is a `fix` task: edit the code and stop. Do not write a summary and do not emit an ANSWER line.
notes: Root cause (shared tenant-lifecycle contract, repository layer): the organization repository does not agree with itself about closed workspaces. Injected (bug.patch, 1 file, 2 defects): findOrgBySlug lost its archived_at IS NULL predicate (comment: the layout decides what to render for a closed workspace) and listOrgsForUser lost the organizations.archived_at filter. Latent in pristine and exercised by the prompt: findOrgById never filtered archived orgs, and every service, job and listener that starts from an org id (notification fan-out, digest builder, invitation acceptance, overdue sweep, trial expiry, webhook delivery, search rebuild, billing planFor, actor resolution by id) therefore keeps operating on a closed workspace; deleteOrganization re-archives an archived org without complaint; closing leaves the subscription trialing (so the trial-expiry job later records billing.plan_changed, which the activity listener and the webhook fan-out pick up) and leaves pending invitations acceptable; notify() falls back to the free plan when the org lookup returns nothing instead of writing nothing. Reference fix (10 files, 3 layers, ~147 changed lines): organization-repository findOrgById live-only by default with an explicit ArchiveScope for the closing path, findOrgBySlug and listOrgsForUser restored, listTakenOrgSlugs deliberately still includes closed orgs (the slug unique index still holds them); organization-service deleteOrganization reads with includeArchived, assertNotArchived (AlreadyArchivedError), cancels the subscription as of the closing time, revokes pending invitations, fails pending webhook deliveries, plus isOrganizationOpen/requireOpenOrganization helpers; webhook-repository failPendingDeliveries; invitation-service acceptInvitation requires an open org; notification-service notify returns nothing when the org is not open; session-service switchActiveOrg refuses a closed org explicitly; overdue-issue-job, trial-expiry-job, search-reindex-job skip closed orgs; webhook-delivery-job fails a closed org's deliveries with an explicit reason. Traps: making every org read live-only "for consistency" turns the taken-slug scan live-only and a new workspace with a closed slug dies on organizations_slug_idx (the prompt requires a different address, not an error); a live-only id lookup alone makes the second closing a not_found instead of the required conflict; notify() must be guarded itself because with a null org it still writes rows under the free-plan fallback; the subscription must end at closing or the trial job downgrades the closed org (its activity listener then records the plan change). Validation: bug -> git apply clean, tsc 0, visible 617/617 (no visible edits needed); hidden 15/16 fail; bug+solution -> hidden 16/16, full 633/633, tsc 0; naive A (revert the two injected reads only) 11/16 fail; naive B (A + findOrgById live-only, nothing else) 8/16 fail; naive C (full solution + taken-slug scan live-only) 1/16 fail with SqliteError UNIQUE organizations.slug; naive D (full solution minus the notify guard) 1/16 fail; hidden x3 stable.
